name: False Cognates
moduleIntroduction: Welcome! This module helps you avoid common mistakes with 'false cognates' (faux amis)—words that look similar in French and English but mean different things. For example, 'actuellement' means 'currently', not 'actually'. These small words can change your meaning completely!
contrastiveExplanation:
Common False Cognates:

• Actually vs. Currently: 'Actuellement' = Currently (now). 'Actually' = In fact/Really.
• Assist vs. Attend: 'Assister à' = Attend (be present). 'Assist' = Help.
• Library vs. Bookstore: 'Librairie' = Bookstore (buy). 'Library' = Bibliothèque (borrow).
• Sensible vs. Sensitive: 'Sensible' (French) = Sensitive (English). 'Sensible' (English) = Reasonable/Logical.
• Deception vs. Disappointment: 'Déception' = Disappointment. 'Deception' = Tricking someone.

commonErrors.wrong: I am actually working at the bank.
commonErrors.correct: I am currently working at the bank.

commonErrors.wrong: I bought a book at the library.
commonErrors.correct: I bought a book at the bookstore.

commonErrors.wrong: She is very sensible to cold.
commonErrors.correct: She is very sensitive to cold.

items.questionText: I want to buy a novel. Where is the ___?
items.feedback: Correct! A 'bookstore' (librairie) is where you buy books. A 'library' is where you borrow them.

items.questionText: I will ___ the meeting at 10 AM.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Attend' means to be present (assister à). 'Assist' means to help.

items.questionText: I am tired. I want to ___ at home.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Je veux rester à la maison...
frenchComparison.englishStructure: I want to stay at home...

visualHighlighting.incorrect: I want to rest at home (different meaning)
visualHighlighting.correct: I want to stay at home

items.questionText: My arm hurts. I ___ myself playing football.
Do you have any ___? I need to buy water.

visualHighlighting.incorrect: Do you have any money (too general)

items.questionText: Put the chair in the ___ of the room.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Coin' (of a room) is 'Corner'. A 'Coin' in English is a metal piece of money (pièce).

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Dans le coin de la pièce...
frenchComparison.englishStructure: In the corner of the room...

items.feedback: Correct! 'Passer un examen' is 'Take an exam'. In English, 'Pass' means you succeeded (réussir).

frenchComparison.whyDifficult: 'Passer un examen' = 'Take an exam'. 'Pass an exam' = 'Réussir un examen'.

visualHighlighting.incorrect: I will pass my exam (implies success)

items.feedback: Correct! The fresh fruit (raisin) is 'grape'. 'Raisin' in English is a dried grape (raisin sec).

items.questionText: He is going to the ___ to buy food.
items.feedback: Correct! A 'store' is a shop (magasin). 'Store' (French) is a 'blind' or 'shade' for a window.

frenchComparison.englishStructure: He is going to the store...

visualHighlighting.incorrect: He is going to the blind
visualHighlighting.correct: He is going to the store

items.questionText: Put on your ___ it is cold.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Veste' is usually 'Jacket'. A 'Vest' in English is a 'gilet' (sleeveless).
Correct! The room (la salle de classe) is 'classroom'. 'Class' is the group of students or the lesson.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Le professeur est dans la classe...
frenchComparison.englishStructure: The teacher is in the classroom...

items.feedback: Correct! The object (assiette) is a 'plate'. 'Plat' (French) refers to the food served (Dish).
Correct! 'Collège' is 'Secondary school' or 'Middle school'. 'College' in English is usually University.

frenchComparison.englishStructure: My daughter is at secondary school...

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Ne marche pas sur le gazon...

items.questionText: I am ___ working as a teacher.
Be careful what you say to him. He is very ___.

frenchComparison.englishStructure: She is a very nice person...

items.questionText: The movie was bad. It was a big ___.
Please ___ the text in two sentences.
We are looking for a ___ for our holiday.

frenchComparison.englishStructure: We are looking for a rental...

items.questionText: Where is the ___? I need to leave.

items.feedback: Correct! 'Mauvais caractère' is 'Bad temper'. 'Character' refers to moral strength or a person in a book.

items.questionText: The ___ for the application is Friday.

items.feedback: Correct! 'Vacances' is 'Vacation' or 'Holiday'. 'Vacancy' means an empty room or job opening (poste vacant).
Correct! 'Formidable' (French) is 'Great' or 'Wonderful'. English 'Formidable' means 'Scary' or 'Impressive' (fearful).
Correct! 'Formation' is 'Training'. English 'Formation' refers to the shape or structure of something.
Correct! 'Une bonne occasion' is often an 'Opportunity'. 'Occasion' in English usually means a specific event.

items.questionText: I visited my parents during the ___.

items.feedback: Correct! To 'ignore' means to pay no attention. 'Ignorer' (French) usually means 'not to know'. This is a tricky one as meanings overlap.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Il n'a pas tenu compte de ma commande...
frenchComparison.whyDifficult: 'Ignorer' usually means 'Not know'. 'Ignore' means 'Pay no attention'.

visualHighlighting.incorrect: He didn't know my order (different meaning)

items.feedback: Correct! 'Supporter' (endure) is 'Tolerate' or 'Stand'. 'Support' means to help or encourage.

items.questionText: I ___ my friend to the airport.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Accompagner' is often 'Take'. 'Accompany' is more formal.
Correct! 'Menu' (repas) is 'Meal'. A 'Menu' in English is the list of food.

items.questionText: He will ___ come to the party.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Éventuellement' is 'Possibly'. 'Eventually' means 'Finally' or 'In the end'.

frenchComparison.englishStructure: He claims to be a doctor...

visualHighlighting.incorrect: He pretends to be a doctor (implies he is not)
visualHighlighting.correct: He claims to be a doctor

items.feedback: Correct! 'Réaliser' (make happen) is 'Achieve'. 'Realize' usually means 'to notice' or 'understand'.

items.questionText: The food was spoiled and he was ___.
I am going to see a ___ about my back pain.
items.feedback: Correct! A doctor is a 'Physician'. A 'Physicist' is a scientist (physicien).

frenchComparison.englishStructure: I am going to see a physician...

items.feedback: Correct! 'Par hasard' is 'By chance'. 'Hazard' means 'Danger' or 'Risk'.
Correct! 'Ignorer' (not know) translates to 'Don't know'. 'Ignore' means 'refuse to listen'.

frenchComparison.englishStructure: I don't know his phone number...

items.questionText: They built a new ___ in the industrial zone.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Ils ont construit une nouvelle fabrique...

items.questionText: Can you give me your ___ on this?
items.feedback: Correct! 'Avis' is 'Opinion'. 'Notice' is a written announcement.

frenchComparison.englishStructure: Can you give me your opinion...

items.feedback: Correct! This one is a true cognate!

items.questionText: He is the ___ of the story.

items.feedback: Correct! 'Injure' (French) is 'Insult'. 'Injury' is a physical wound.
Trick question. 'Habit' in English is a routine. 'Habit' (clothes) is French.
Correct! 'Un prix intéressant' is 'An attractive price'. 'Interesting' is for books/ideas.
Correct! 'Misère' can mean poverty, but often just 'problems/trouble'. 'Misery' means deep unhappiness.

frenchComparison.englishStructure: He has a lot of problems...

items.feedback: Correct! 'Réviser' is often 'Review'. 'Revise' means to change/edit.

visualHighlighting.incorrect: I will revise my notes (edit them)

items.questionText: There was a long ___ at the bank.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Il y avait une grande affluence...

items.questionText: I borrowed a book from the ___.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Library' is where you borrow books.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: J'ai emprunté un livre à la bibliothèque...

items.questionText: Can you ___ me with this bag?
The teacher ___ the students to be quiet.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Ask' is polite. 'Demand' is too strong.

items.questionText: We ___ at a hotel in Kribi.

visualHighlighting.incorrect: We rested at a hotel (implies sleeping)

items.feedback: Correct! 'Gardez la monnaie' is 'Keep the change'.

items.feedback: Correct! 'Coin' is a piece of metal money.
Correct! 'Pass' means you got a good grade (reussir). 'Take' means you sat for it.

frenchComparison.frenchStructure: Elle a acheté un nouveau soutien-gorge...

items.feedback: Correct! A window covering is a 'blind'. 'Store' is a shop.

Correct! 'University' is for higher education. 'College' in US English is also University.
